sections.h2: Why Fairborn sales follow their own calendar
sections.html:
Fairborn demand tracks Wright State University and the Wright-Patterson Air Force Base workforce, so it moves with academic terms and military assignments. A seller who needs a closing date ahead of the next move can pick a cash buyer, a listing or a by-owner sale, and the choice should match the condition of the house.

  • Listing: reaches the widest group of buyers, then waits on financing and appraisal.
  • By owner: keeps the agent's fee, with every showing and form on your plate.
  • Cash purchase: fits worn systems, rental turnover problems or an estate, because the buyer takes the house as it is.

Fairborn is a Dayton suburb in Greene County, and the Greene County Auditor handles the deed transfer. The median resident was 34.0 years old at the 2020 census, a young population that keeps some rentals turning over often.

Fairborn's population is 35,754 for July 1, 2025, up 3.7 percent from 2020. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $175,000, and owners live in 51.2 percent of homes. The 2020 count shows 15,601 households and 16,707 housing units.

  • Median gross rent: $977
  • Households: 15,911, averaging 2.14 people
  • Median household income: $61,751

The city levies a 2.0 percent income tax plus a 0.5 percent school district tax. If you're moving out of town, ask a tax preparer how that changes what you owe. Of the city's 14.725 square miles, 8.864 are zoned residential, and the Historic Osborn District holds some of the oldest houses. Buyers of older homes ask about foundations, roofs and past moves or repairs.

Fairborn enforces a property maintenance code in Part Thirteen, Title Five of its codified ordinances. It covers siding, broken windows, gutters, roofs, walls, foundations, sidewalks, sheds, garages, fences and debris, and it reaches stored materials and vehicles parked in the yard. A violation notice on your address can complicate a closing, so deal with it early.

  • Reports and complaints: the city's 24 hour line is 937-318-1605. Illegally parked vehicles and noise go to the Police non-emergency line, 937-754-3000.
  • Assessments: the Finance Department has an Assessment Inquiry Form so a buyer or seller can ask whether special assessments are attached to a parcel.
  • Abandoned property: the Property Maintenance Division asks neighbors to help identify vacant, unsecured buildings.

Fairborn lies in Greene County, so the Auditor's office transfers the deed and charges the transfer and conveyance fees. Call the Real Estate Department at (937) 562-5072 with questions.

Greene County Auditor deed transfer requirements
Deed requirementWhat the Auditor needs
Statement of valueDTE 100 or DTE 100 (EX) with the deed
Grantor nameMust read as it did on the previous deed
Map departmentApproves and initials the deed before the Auditor sees it
SignatureGrantor signs, and the deed is notarized
Conveyance fee$2.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price
Parcel transfer fee$0.50 per parcel

The Auditor's website carries a conveyance fee calculator, so ask your title company to run it.

Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 requires a signed disclosure form for homes with one to four units. A buyer who receives the form after signing may rescind within three business days, and no later than the earlier of 30 days after acceptance or closing. A seller who inherited the property and did not live in it during the prior year is exempt, which removes one task from the list.

sections.h2: Selling a Fairborn rental or inherited house
sections.html:
A quick sale often fits a rental with a turnover problem or an inherited house with a distant owner. Before you sign with anyone, gather these items:

  • A written offer showing the price, the closing date and who pays each fee.
  • Proof of funds from a cash buyer, or a lender's letter from a financed one.
  • The Greene County Auditor's conveyance figure, which your title company can run through the county calculator.
  • Any city violation notice, assessment inquiry response or tenant lease that touches the address.

If a tenant lives in the house, read the lease for the end date and notice terms, and tell buyers early. A student or base renter may leave on a predictable date, which can be a selling point for an investor.

Because buyers here include students, faculty and service members, the best weeks to list often line up with academic terms and assignment cycles. A house that appeals to a family transferring to the base may sit idle during a slow stretch, while a rental near campus can draw interest from investors at almost any time. If your date is fixed, a cash buyer takes the calendar out of the equation.

Population has been rising, yet neighboring Beavercreek is larger, so buyers often compare more than one town before they commit. Price against recent Fairborn sales, ask for more than one offer so you can see the spread, and keep every written offer for comparison.

sections.h2: Paperwork to collect before you list
sections.html:
Gather the deed, so you can confirm the grantor name matches exactly, along with the latest tax bill, the state disclosure form and any lease. Add receipts for roof, siding, gutter or foundation work, since the property maintenance code covers those items and buyers ask about them. If you have received a city notice, bring proof that it was resolved.

Submit an Assessment Inquiry Form early if you aren't sure whether a special assessment is attached to the parcel. A buyer who learns about one at the last minute may ask for a price cut, while a seller who finds it first can plan for it.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Fairborn
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, the title company searches the record, confirms the grantor name matches the prior deed, and sends the deed through the Auditor's map department. Ask the city's Finance Department about assessments on the parcel and the Property Maintenance Division about any open notice at the same time, so the title search holds no surprises.

At the signing, the grantor signs and the deed is notarized. Bring photo identification, payoff letters for any mortgage, and a lease if the house is rented. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, which can bring the closing date forward. The same deed steps and county fees apply either way, so settle in writing who pays each charge before you agree to the price.

faqs.q: What does the Greene County Auditor charge to transfer a deed?
faqs.a: The county charges a conveyance fee of $2.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price and $0.50 per parcel. Use the county's conveyance fee calculator for your actual figure.

faqs.q: Whom do I call about a property maintenance problem in Fairborn?
faqs.a: Call the city's 24 hour hotline at 937-318-1605. Parking and noise complaints go to the Fairborn Police Department non-emergency line at 937-754-3000.

faqs.q: Can a Fairborn buyer find out about assessments on a parcel?
faqs.a: Yes. The Finance Department accepts an Assessment Inquiry Form from people considering a purchase, and a representative responds with the assessment details.

faqs.q: Is the Fairborn income tax rate the same after a move out of the city?
faqs.a: No. The city levies a 2.0 percent income tax and a 0.5 percent school district tax on residents, so a move to another municipality can change what you owe. Ask a tax preparer about your situation.

faqs.q: What is a typical home value in Fairborn?
faqs.a: The median for owner-occupied homes is $175,000. Condition, size and distance from the campus and the base move your own number, so check recent nearby sales and ask for more than one offer.
